diagnosis: The canonical BVE round drained the root and built its schedule once, then kept attempting candidates after a declined one had changed solver state. A candidate installs its unit resolvents immediately and they survive its later growth decline, so later candidates ran at an incomplete root closure against a stale schedule. The last one was the very pivot the unit had fixed: its general-definition refutation re-derived the root literal the kernel already held and tripped the definition-unit precondition.
fix: Every BVE candidate is owed an unassigned pivot and a complete root closure, asserted at candidate entry. bve_eliminate reports a decline that changed state, and the canonical round ends with Ok at the first candidate that changes state, so the next application re-drains and re-schedules; a stale attempt is impossible by construction. DefaultPolicy never enters the canonical round (it doses one-instance applications and propagates/flushes after each as Kissat does), so its trajectories are unchanged.
